title: Self-discovering RL in the Era of Experience: Is Learning History an Asset or a Burden?
abstract: arXiv:2609.35897v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The pursuit of recursive self-improvement (RSI) toward general intelligence is divided between macro-level language model scaling and the interaction-driven principles of "Era of Experience". Yet, any self-improving architecture ultimately rests upon its underlying optimization engine: if general intelligence requires learning from grounded interaction, the reinforcement learning (RL) update rule itself must be capable of cumulative adaptation. While algorithm self-discovery has produced Disco103 that surpassed PPO to achieve SOTA benchmark performance -- its internal update machinery remains an uninspected black box. We present the first causal mechanistic audit of a self-discovered RL rule, structured directly around the five pillars of the Era of Experience: extended horizon, grounded reward scales, continuing streams, within-lifetime change, and exploration depth. translated_title: 体验时代中的自发现强化学习：学习历史是资产还是负担？
translated_abstract: 迈向通用智能的递归自我改进（RSI）研究分为宏观层面的语言模型扩展与“体验时代”的交互驱动原则两条路径。然而，任何自我改进的架构最终都建立在其底层优化引擎之上：如果通用智能需要从真实交互中学习，那么强化学习（RL）的更新规则本身必须具备累积适应的能力。尽管算法自我发现已经产生了超越PPO并达到SOTA基准性能的Disco103——但其内部的更新机制仍然是一个未经检验的黑箱。我们围绕“体验时代”的五大支柱——扩展视界、真实交互奖励尺度、持续数据流、生命周期内的变化和探索深度——对自我发现的RL规则进行了首次因果机制审计。通过手术式地固定、冻结和移植循环状态……
tldr: 该论文首次对自我发现的强化学习规则Disco103进行了因果机制审计，围绕体验时代的五大支柱剖析其内部更新机制，以探究学习历史究竟是强化学习性能的资产还是负担。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first causal mechanistic audit of a self-discovered RL rule (Disco103), structured around the five pillars of the Era of Experience, to determine whether learning history is an asset or a burden for reinforcement learning performance.
